title: How Long Can Breast Milk Sit Out? | Feed Flow
description: The CDC says fresh breast milk keeps 4 hours at room temperature and 4 days in the fridge. Frozen, 6 months is best and 12 acceptable. Leftovers differ.
h1: How long can breast milk sit out?
intro: The CDC says freshly pumped breast milk can sit out for up to 4 hours at 77°F (25°C) or colder, keep up to 4 days in the fridge, and keep about 6 months in the freezer (up to 12 is acceptable). Thawed milk that has been warmed, and milk left in the bottle after a feed, should be used within 2 hours. The UK's NHS is stricter on leftovers (1 hour) and allows longer in a fridge at 4°C or lower (up to 8 days).

faqs: How long can breast milk sit out after pumping?

The CDC says freshly pumped breast milk can stay at room temperature, 77°F or colder, for up to 4 hours. The Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine says 4 hours is best, and 6 to 8 hours may be reasonable for very clean milk in a cooler room. The NHS page gives no room temperature time.
Can I reuse breast milk my baby didn't finish?

The CDC says to use leftover milk within 2 hours, then discard it. The NHS says to use it within 1 hour of your baby drinking from the bottle and throw away anything left over. The Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine says 1 to 2 hours after the feed ends.
How long is breast milk good in the fridge?
The CDC says up to 4 days. The NHS says up to 8 days at 4°C or lower, or within 3 days if you are unsure of your fridge's temperature or it runs between 5 and 10°C.
Can you refreeze thawed breast milk?
The CDC and the NHS both say not to refreeze breast milk once it has thawed. The Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine says there is too little research to make a recommendation.
How long is thawed breast milk good for?

The CDC says to use milk thawed in the fridge within 24 hours, counted from when it is fully thawed, and within 2 hours once it is at room temperature or warmed. The NHS says to use defrosted milk straight away.
